Clopine CentralTM offers haematology advice for any consumer on Clozapine therapy. The

An on-call haematologist at Clopine CentralTM can be contacted on 1800 656 403 for advice.
eCPMSTM offers information via a cardiovascular referral for a patient on Clozaril who needs
cardiology input. Medical information can be contacted on 1800 931 383.
Additional blood tests including Clozapine levels may be requested based on additional
monitoring requirements or at the discretion of the treating doctor.

3.4. Admission of a Patient Currently Treated with Clozapine

3.4.1. When a patient currently treated with clozapine is admitted to hospital, ascertain
whether the patient is continuing therapy or the patient has been admitted due to a side
effect of clozapine treatment (e.g. agranulocytosis, myocarditis). If a decision is made to
cease or withhold clozapine this should be made in consultation with the treating Mental
Health team wherever possible. Refer to section 3.7 Discontinuation of Therapy.

Clozapine Prescribing, Administering and Monitoring

Vigilant haematological and physical health monitoring is an ongoing requirement for patients
taking Clozapine. This includes regular monitoring of a patient full blood count, monitoring for
constipation and gastrointestinal hypomotility and for metabolic and cardiac side effects.

The Australian Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) with many other countries around the
world mandate regular haematological monitoring and patient tracking to minimise the risk of
Clozapine side effects. This is achieved by enrolling every patient taking Clozapine onto a
mandatory patient monitoring system (Clopine CentralTM for patients prescribed Clopine® and
eCPMSTM for patients prescribed Clozaril®).

Both centres offer protocols and product information.

The risk of developing agranulocytosis and neutropenia is closely monitored by mandatory
testing and entry of White Cell Count (WCC) and Absolute Neutrophil Count (ANC) onto the
patient monitoring system. This is performed:

8.2 Monitoring for agranulocytosis and neutropenia
WBC & ANC must be monitored weekly for the first 18 weeks of treatment and 4 weekly thereafter
for the duration of treatment. More frequent monitoring is required as per the monitoring protocol
if WBC and/or ANC declines or if the patient exhibits clinical symptoms of infection (e.g. fever,
sore throat).
